newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Supreme Court says will not question Gonzalez.
newsitem.headline: Spain Supreme Court says will not question Gonzalez.

text.p: Spain's Supreme Court decided on Tuesday not to question former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez about a 1980s "dirty war" on Basque rebels in which 28 people were killed.
After six hours of closed-doors deliberations by 10 judges, Justice Jose Augusto de Vega told reporters the top tribunal had decided against calling the Socialist leader.
State radio said the decision appeared to have been the result of a split vote, with four of the 10 justices in favour of questioning Gonzalez.

State prosecutors told the Supreme Court on Monday they saw no grounds to call the former prime minister, who lost elections in March after 13 years in power, but that this could change if new evidence emerged.

Gonzalez denies charges by former security chiefs and disgruntled associates that he knew of the campaign of bombings, kidnappings, torture and murder against presumed separatists from ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
